title: Declarative traffic manifests and SDK safety operators for model rollouts
creator: Avery Collins
description:
Summary:
This ticket specifies a declarative "traffic manifest" schema plus a small set of SDK 'safety operator' helpers to make canaries, A/B tests, and shadow traffic easier to implement and safer. The goal is to provide: 1) a human-readable, versionable manifest users can commit and pin to repos or apply via the Console/API; 2) idempotent, replay-safe SDK hooks that implement holdback/percentage ramps and shadow probes; and 3) a compact permission model for who can apply manifests and who can approve auto-rollouts or rollbacks.

Problem/Context:
Current rollout tooling is split across the Console UI, low-level rollout API primitives, and per-SDK client helpers. Customers ask for a declarative artifact they can store alongside CI (so rollouts are reviewed like code), and for SDK helpers that implement safe default behaviors (idempotent apply, backoff retry, and local canary emulation for offline testing). We also need stronger guardrails for shadow traffic and auto-rollback triggers so teams do not accidentally flood downstream telemetry or violate data residency.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Declarative manifest vs. purely imperative API: We chose a YAML/JSON manifest so teams can review rollouts in PRs, gate with CI, and pin a manifest to a deployment commit. Trade-off: adds a reconciliation step in control plane (apply -> reconciler) but reduces manual errors.
- Idempotency surface: manifests include an "apply_id" UUID. The SDK helpers accept an optional client-provided idempotency token for programmatic applies. We avoid server-side only tokens to make retries predictable across client restarts.
- Shadowing semantics: two modes: "noop-shadow" (send copy without incrementing traffic metrics) and "metric-shadow" (send copy and include shadow metrics but mark them separately). Default is noop-shadow to avoid metric pollution.
- Auto-rollback policy: declarative threshold-based triggers (error_rate > X over rolling window OR latency_p95 regression > Y OR eval-quality-drop > Z). Can configure a grace period and escalations. We will not enable auto-rollback by default; manifests must opt-in explicitly.

Manifest schema (high level):
- metadata: name, team, apply_id, description, created_by
- target: model_id, model_variant (pinned), region_filters
- traffic: strategy (canary|ab|blue_green|shadow), steps (list of percentages + duration), holdback_percent
- safety: auto_rollback: { enabled, conditions: [{metric, comparator, threshold, window_secs}], cooldown_secs }
- observability: required_metrics: [latency_p95, error_rate, quality_score_id]
- permissions: approvers: [roles|users], apply_roles_required_to_promote

SDK safety operators (client helpers):
- applyManifest(manifest, opts) -- idempotent across retries using apply_id. Returns an operation id and provides a local progress stream.
- probeShadow(requestPayload, opts) -- sends a copy to shadow targets with toggles for noop vs metric-shadow and respects data-sanitization hooks.
- holdbackClient.wrap(fn, opts) -- wraps a model call in a local holdback that mirrors production split for offline testing (useful for integration tests).
- evaluateAndDecide(opId, metricsSnapshot) -- client-side helper that fetches server rollout state and submits a promotion or rollback suggestion (requires appropriate permission).

Permissions and audit:
- Manifests carry an "apply_roles_required_to_promote" list. Applying a manifest can be done by engineers, but promoting beyond canary requires approver role or a signed approval token.
- All manifest operations create immutable audit events with the apply_id, operator, and git-commit (if provided).

Telemetry and SLO integration:
- We will require customers to wire at least one objective metric in the manifest (latency_p95 or error_rate or quality_score). The reconciler will fail manifest apply if required metrics are not provisioned for the target model.
- Rollout evaluator will compute deltas vs baseline and emit events: rollout.evaluation.{pass|fail|drift}. These will feed Console charts and alerting rules.

Implementation notes and acceptance criteria:
- Backend: add a lightweight reconciler that accepts manifests and stores manifest state keyed by apply_id. Reconciler performs validation, creates rollout operation, and emits operation id.
- API: POST /v1/manifests: validate and enqueue. GET /v1/manifests/{apply_id}/ops for progress and events.
- SDK: provide JS and Python helpers implementing idempotency, apply backoff, local holdbacks, and shadow probes.
- RBAC: new roles: rollout.approver, rollout.angler (can apply but not promote).

updates: 2025-02-14: Initial PM stub + informal design reviewed with Eng (Ravi, Lina). Decided on apply_id approach for idempotency.
2025-02-20: Security review kickoff. Data-sanitization hook for shadow traffic required. Recorded requirement in this ticket.
2025-02-24: UX meeting: manifest preview in Console will show a dry-run and required metrics. Add UI flag for 'enable_auto_rollback' opt-in.
2025-02-28: Eng design doc drafted (link: https://drive.redwood.company/docs/rollout-manifest-design) and PR created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/4821).
2025-03-01: Scoped SDK MVP: JS + Python helpers, with later owners for Go and Java SDKs. Added to release runtime-1.21.
acceptance_criteria: Users can submit a traffic manifest and receive an operation id; repeated submits with same apply_id are treated idempotently.
Console shows manifest dry-run and required-metric validation errors before apply.
SDK helpers expose applyManifest and probeShadow with documented behavior; examples exist in SDK repo README.
Auto-rollback can be enabled per-manifest and fires an immutable event when triggered.
Audit logs contain apply_id, git commit, actor, and final outcome for every rollout operation.
Security review sign-off confirming shadow probe sanitization and RBAC matrix.
notes: Engineering owners: Ravi Shah (PM lead), Lina Ortega (Eng lead). Follow-up tasks: ENG-... will implement reconciler and API; SDK owners to own helper libraries. Aim: pilot with two internal teams (billing and search) then public beta.
